summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: This bill is part of a package that creates a legislative framework for national automated identity matching services used by government and industry.

The package would authorise one-to-one identity checks with consent through the Document Verification Service and Face Verification Service, and one-to-many matching only to protect legally assumed identities.
Around 2.6 million Face Verification Service transactions occurred in the 2022-23 financial year, and the bill would impose privacy safeguards including consent, breach reporting and annual audits.
changes: Authorises public and private entities to use one-to-one identity matching services with the individual's consent.
Prohibits one-to-many facial matching except to protect legally assumed identities such as undercover officers.
Allows the Attorney-General's Department to develop and operate the identity verification facilities.
Creates offences for unauthorised recording, disclosure or access of protected information by entrusted persons.
Requires state and territory authorities to inform individuals if their data is stored on the National Driver Licence Facial Recognition Solution.
Establishes annual compliance reporting and assessments by the Information Commissioner.
summary.affected: Government agencies, private sector entities including banks, and individuals whose identity is verified through the services.

This amendment was introduced by Griffith MP [Max Chandler-Mather](https://theyvoteforyou.org.au/people/representatives/griffith/max_chandler-mather) (Greens). ### Amendment text > *That all words after "That" be omitted with a view to substituting the following words:* > > *"the House declines to give the bill a second reading until the Privacy Act reforms are in place in recognition of the significant privacy and data implications of this proposal".*

The majority voted in favour of a [motion](https://www.openaustralia.org.au/debates/?id=2023-10-18.58.1) to agree with the bill's main idea. In parliamentary jargon, they voted to read the bill for a second time. This means they can now consider it in more detail. ### What is the bill's main idea? According to the [bills digest](https://www.aph.gov.au/Parliamentary_Business/Bills_Legislation/bd/bd2324a/24bd24) (which is prepared by the non-partisan parliamentary library): > *Bills with similar purposes were introduced in 2018 and 2019 but lapsed with the dissolution of the House of Representatives in April 2019 and April 2022, respectively. ... The Identity Verification Services Bill 2023 (IVS Bill), as outlined in the Explanatory Memorandum, would:* > > * *authorise 1:1 matching of identity through the identity verification services, with consent of the relevant individual, by public and private sector entities.
